BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

 IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                           )
 EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                                  )
 REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                         )   Docket No. 25-00082-UT
 PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                             )


                                      PROCEDURAL ORDER

        THIS MATTER comes before Jocelyn Barrett and Elizabeth C. Hurst, hearing examiners

for the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”), upon the Application of El

Paso Electric Company (“EPE”), the Commission’s Order Appointing Co-Hearing Examiners

issued on April 2, 2026, and the Commission’s Rules of Procedure 1.2.2.24 and 1.2.2.29 NMAC.

Being duly informed, the Hearing Examiners FIND AND CONCLUDE:

        1.      On December 4, 2025, EPE filed a request for variance to file its audit report

(Schedule Q-6) for calendar year 2024 around mid-April 2026 which would be part of the filing

package for revision of its rates. The Commission granted the request for variance on December

18, 2025. 1

        2.      On February 6, 2026, EPE requested a variance from the 150-day requirement of

Rule 17.9.530.7(F) NMAC, seeking a four-week extension to file its rate case, up to and including

March 27, 2026, to finalize its rate case package in order to ensure that the filing is proper and

accurate. 2

        3.      On February 19, 2026, the Commission issued an Order Granting Extension of

Time, granting EPE the four-week extension to file its rate case.



    1 Order Granting Variance (December 18, 2025).


    2 EPE’s Unopposed and Verified Motion for Variance Regarding Rate Case Filing Deadline (Feb. 6, 2026).


    Docket No. 25-00082-UT
    Procedural Order
    Page 1 of 7
             BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Procedural Order                                      Docket No. 25-00082-UT


          4.   On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates

under Advice Notice No. 317 containing EPE’s proposed rates.

          5.   On April 2, 2026, the Commission appointed Jocelyn Barrett and Elizabeth Hurst

as Co-Hearing Examiners. In the same order the Commission amended the case caption of this

docket.

          6.   On April 8, 2026, EPE filed a Notice of Filing of Supplemental Schedule Q-6 –

The Independent Accountant’s Review Report for EPE for the calendar year 2024.

          7.   EPE asserts that conditions have materially changed since approval of its current

base rates in Case No. 20-00104-UT, necessitating an adjustment to reflect significant post-Test-

Year investments, inflationary impacts, and increased service demands. EPE’s updated cost of

service identifies a $70.6 million non-fuel base rate revenue deficiency, resulting in a requested

net revenue increase of $70.4 million and supported by a proposed weighted average cost of capital

of 8.35 percent. The proposed increase is designed to recover approximately $2.4 billion in total

company investment—$408.44 million attributable to New Mexico—including substantial

additions to distribution, transmission, generation, nuclear, and general plant, as well as

Commission-approved costs associated with the advanced metering system program and battery

energy storage facility agreements. 3 There are also proposed tariff revisions including Data Center

Tariff Rates and three new rate options including: low-income, off-peak TOD, and a 2 year peak

time rebate pilot program.

          8.   The Application and supporting documents are accessible online on EPE’s website,

https://www.epelectric.com/company/public-notices and on the Commission’s PRCe360



   3 Application at 2 (March 27, 2026).

Affairs – NM.

       9.       On April 15, 2026, EPE filed a Notice of Errata and Filing of Replacement Exhibits

(“Notice of Errata”). In the Notice of Errata, EPE stated it discovered or was made aware that there

were several errors in its initial Application filing. Specifically, the errors included: a wrong

document filed, incorrect formatting, and, most significantly, missing workpapers. EPE requested

the corrected pages attached to its Notice of Errata, which amounted to over 1,600 pages, are

substituted for the incorrect versions filed with EPE’s Application.

       10.      The Hearing Examiners held a Prehearing Conference on April 16, 2026, at 10:00

a.m. to create a procedural schedule for the adjudication. Attending the prehearing were

representatives of EPE, Commission Staff, Federal Executive Agencies, City of Las Cruces, Doña

Ana County, NMSU, CCAE, New Mexico Department of Justice, Prosperity Works, WRA, as well

as individual EPE ratepayers.

       11.      The Commission issued its Order Suspending Advice Notice No. 317 on April 23,

2026, that set forth that EPE Advice Notice 317 was suspended for nine months beginning May

15, 2026, and stated that the Commission may extend the suspension period an additional three

months should it determine more time is necessary to resolve this matter.

       12.      That schedule along with the other matters discussed at the prehearing are adopted

as ordered below.

Procedural Order                                      Docket No. 25-00082-UT


IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       A.      As soon as practicable, but no later than June 5, 2026, EPE shall (at its sole expense)

(1) mail the approved Notice attached here as Attachment A to customers by bill stuffer or email

(if the customer has enrolled in electronic/digital billing) The font size in the mailing shall not

be smaller than the equivalent to a Times New Roman 10.5 font size; (2) publish the notice

once in newspapers of general circulation in every county where EPE provides service in New

Mexico; (3) as soon as practicable post the application and notice on its website in a location that

is maximally visible to customers and likely to be seen by them.

       B.      EPE shall utilize social media to the maximum extent practicable to alert its

customers to the existence of this proceeding and the rates proposed. To the extent social media

requires modification to the approved notice or only a link to that notice, this is approved.

       C.      EPE shall file promptly in this docket an affidavit confirming it completed the

forms of mailing, publication, and posting identified above.

       D.      The Notice will also be posted on the Legal Notices section of the Commission’s

website https://www.prc.nm.gov/nmprc-legal-notices/.

       E.      People desiring to intervene in this case must file a motion for leave to intervene

that conforms to 1.2.2.23(A) and 1.2.2.23(B) NMAC by June 22, 2026.

       F.      Any dispositive motion—a motion to dismiss, any motion that would (as a matter

of law) resolve some portion of this case or require the applicant to retract and refile the

Application, or any motion that would result in summary rejection of any portion of the

Application—must be filed by June 29, 2026. This dispositive motion deadline is established to

ensure the proceedings are efficient, and that any energy dedicated to establishing the application

is patently deficient in some way is expended early in the proceedings before the case turns to

competing evidence of what constitutes the most optimal outcome.

        G.     Staff and intervenor direct testimony shall be filed by July 24, 2026.

        H.     Any stipulation and supporting documents pursuant to 1.2.2.20 NMAC may be

filed by August 7, 2026. Opposition to stipulation shall be filed by August 12, 2026.

        I.     Rebuttal testimony or in the alternative, testimony in support of a stipulation, shall

be filed by August 19, 2026. Testimony in opposition to a stipulation shall be filed by August 28,

2026.

        J.     A prehearing conference is tentatively set for September 9, 2026, beginning at

10:00 a.m. MT via the Zoom videoconference platform.

        K.     The public evidentiary hearing will begin on September 21 and continue through

October 2, 2026, beginning each day at 9 a.m. MT. The hearing will be conducted via the Zoom

videoconference platform. The hearing will be livestreamed on YouTube and will be displayed on

the Commission’s website at https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-hearings/.

        L.     People filing prepared testimony consistent with 1.2.2.35(I) NMAC on behalf of a

party shall attend the hearing and submit to examination under oath.

        M.     The procedural dates and requirements set out here are subject to change. Hearings

are occasionally rescheduled or canceled.

        N.     The Commission’s Rules of Procedure 1.2.2 NMAC apply except as modified by

order of the Commission or Hearing Examiners. These and other rules are available online at

https://srca.nm.gov/nmac-home/nmac-titles/.

        O.     People who are not associated with a party to this case may make written or oral

comment as allowed by Rule 1.2.2.23(F) NMAC. Written comments must refer to Docket Number

       Q.      All filings shall be emailed to the Hearing Examiners on the date filed at

Jocelyn.Barrett@prc.nm.gov and Elizabeth.Hurst@prc.nm.gov by no later than 5:00 p.m. MT.

Filing emailed to the Hearing Examiners shall include the Word or other native version of the filing

(e.g., Excel or Power Point) if created in such format. All PDF documents shall be Optical

Character Recognition (“OCR”) enabled. Any filings not emailed to the Hearing Examiners in

compliance with the requirements of this order and Commission rules are subject to being

summarily rejected and stricken from the record at the Hearing Examiners’ discretion.

       R.      Discovery matters and disputes shall be governed by the Commission’s discovery

rules at 1.2.2.25 NMAC. Agreements between or among any of the participants regarding

discovery matters is encouraged. All other participants shall be notified of such agreements.

Motions regarding discovery disputes will not be considered unless accompanied by a statement

that the participants made a good faith effort to resolve the dispute but were unable to do so.

                        NOTICE TO EPE CUSTOMERS

El Paso Electric Company (“EPE”) has filed an Application with the New Mexico Public
Regulation Commission, requesting approval of revised New Mexico retail electric base
rates. EPE states that the $70.6 million non-fuel base rate revenue deficiency shown in EPE’s
proposed cost of service demonstrates the need for a 50.4% base rate base increase, which
is offset by a $0.2 million reduction in miscellaneous service revenue, for a net operating
revenue increase of $70.4 million in these New Mexico revenues. EPE is requesting an 8.35%
weighted cost of capital, a return on equity of 10.7% and an equity to debt capital structure
of 55.5% and 45.5%. According to EPE, the increase is required to recover costs for EPE’s
$408.44 million investment since its 2020 rate case, including investments in distribution,
transmission, nuclear production, local generating plants and general plant. EPE is also
proposing to include in base rates its Commission approved advanced metering system
(“AMS”), and the annual capacity costs associated with Commission approved agreements
for three battery energy storage facilities.

NO ACTION IS REQUIRED ON YOUR PART UNLESS YOU WANT TO BECOME
            A PARTY OR COMMENT ON THE APPLICATION
EPE’s proposed revised rates, set forth in Advice Notice No. 317, would, if approved, affect
all retail classifications. To moderate the rate impact on certain customer classes, EPE has
proposed to voluntarily phase in recovery through a two-part implementation process for
base rates for Rate Nos. 01 (Residential), 05 (Irrigation), 10B (Military), 12 (Private Lighting),
25 (Outdoor Lighting), and 26 (State University). EPE proposed that the first phase, expected
to take effect on January 1, 2027, represents a system average increase of 26.8% for these
rate classes; and the second phase, proposed to take effect on October 1, 2027, reflects an
additional 18.6% increase relative to Phase 1.
 EPE states that the bill impact of the proposed base rate changes will be offset by an
anticipated reduction in Renewable Portfolio Standard (“RPS”) costs. The proposed
increases will be to both the customer charge and the energy charge rates. For example, EPE
projects that a residential customer using an average of 750 kWh during a summer month,
would have a combined impact of a bill increase of 22.5% in Phase 1 followed by an
additional increase of 28.2% in Phase 2, effectively totaling 57.0%. EPE’s proposed increase
in non-fuel base rates represents an increase of $24.62 in Phase 1 followed by an additional
increase of $30.38 per summer month in Phase 2, totaling $55.00. The combined impact of
the proposed base rate changes and the RPS cost reduction for a residential customer using
an average of 500 kWh during a winter month will be a bill increase of 14.5% in Phase 1
followed by an additional increase of 28.6% in Phase 2, effectively totaling 47.3%. EPE’s
proposed increase in non-fuel base rates represents an increase of $10.83 in Phase 1
followed by an additional increase of $17.13 per winter month in Phase 2, totaling $27.96.

EPE is also proposing to implement customer rate options that include: (i) a new Low-
Income Rider to qualified households in the Residential Service Rate the credits the
customer charge dollar for dollar; (ii) experimental off-peak and time-of-day (“TOD”)
demand rates designed to further incentivize certain commercial customers to shift load
from peak hours; (iii) and a new two-year Peak Time Rebate Pilot Program intended to
incentivize Residential Service Rate customers to shift to off-peak usage times by providing
pilot participants the opportunity to receive a bill credit for reducing energy consumption
during peak periods following a notification from EPE. EPE has also proposed new Large
Load Tariff Schedules Rate No. 50 and 51.

Additionally, EPE asks the Commission to:

1. Authorize several design changes to (i) align recovery of demand energy and customer
   costs with how those costs are incurred, thereby minimizing intra-class subsidization,
   (ii) provide customers with accurate price signals that convey cost differences between
   seasonal and non-seasonal time periods to encourage energy conservation and
   potentially reduce customer contribution to EPE’s system peak, (iii) promote stability,
   and (iv) allow EPE the opportunity to recover the costs of providing safe and reliable
   service.
 2. Authorize the proposed replacement of its Rule No. 8 Line Extension Policy and related
   revisions to its Rule 13 Increase or Decrease of Connected Load.
3. Authorize the inclusion in base rates the capacity costs already incurred under the
   Commission-approved Buena Vista 1 Power Purchase Agreement since that resource
   came online in 2023.

class under Advice Notice No. 317 proposed by EPE.

EPE’s complete Application and supporting documents is accessible online on EPE’s
website, https://www.epelectric.com/company/public-notices and the Commission’s

The major events for public participation in this matter will occur as follows:

           Deadline to file motions to intervene to become a party: June 22, 2026
           Deadline to file intervenors’ direct testimony: July 24, 2026
           Deadline to file rebuttal testimony: August 19, 2026



                                    PUBLIC HEARING
A public hearing to hear and receive testimony, exhibits, and legal argument is set for
September 21 – October 2, 2026, commencing at 9:00 a.m. each day. The hearing will be
 conducted online and can be viewed via livestream on the Commission’s YouTube channel
and its website, https://www.prc.nm.gov/public-hearings/. Please contact the Commission
for confirmation of the hearing, because hearings are occasionally cancelled or
rescheduled.

                                     PUBLIC COMMENT

People who are not associated with a party to this case may make written or oral comment
as allowed by Rule 1.2.2.23(F) NMAC. Written comments must refer to Docket Number 25-
00082-UT and be submitted before the Commission makes a final decision. Written
comments and any other filings should be submitted online through PRCe360 Docketing
System. Comments can also be sent via US mail to PRC Records P.O. Box 1269, Santa Fe,
NM 87504.

Alternatively, oral public comment is also welcome during Commission open meetings. The
open meeting schedule can be found at www.prc.nm.gov/nmprc-open-meeting-agenda/.
Email public.comment@prc.nm.gov or call (505) 490-7910 to sign up to comment online or
by phone at an open meeting. If the Commission determines a separate hearing should be
set for oral comments for this matter, the date, time, and location will be announced on the
Commission’s website, https://www.prc.nm.gov/.

Instructions to submit written public comment online, to file pleadings and other
documents,       and     to     view       Commission         dockets       are     found      at
https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/#/public/nm-prc/en/home. All filings subject to
deadlines must be submitted within regular business hours of the due date to be considered timely
filed.

                                    TO BECOME A PARTY

If you wish to appear in this case as a party, you must file a motion for leave to intervene, pursuant
to 1.2.2.23 NMAC, on or before June 22, 2026. Intervenors must become familiar with the rules
regarding practicing before the Commission and all other applicable rules.

The Commission’s Rules of Procedure 1.2.2 NMAC apply except as modified by order of the
Commission or hearing examiners. These and other rules are available online at
https://srca.nm.gov/nmac-home/nmac-titles/.
